To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the internal energy flow analysis of a single effect sorbent heat pump is a very powerful tool that allows to: (1) determine the level of exergy downgrading in the system; (2) determine the level and the location of excess exergy produced in the system; and (3) identify the untapped exergy that can be upgraded by adding an additional effect.
the internal exergy flow analysis of a single effect sorptive heat pump allows the identification of the exergy flow paths and the definition of the exergy flows that can be upgraded or downgraded.
the excess and untapped energies are not equal to the energy not used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study and development of a sorption heat transformer.
the analysis of energy flows within the sorption heat pump, in order to improve its efficiency and to optimize its design.
the development of an exergy analysis methodology that allows the designer to optimize a sorption system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single-effect sorption heat pump is not able to provide a COP larger than 2.
a system based on the internal energy flux recycling can be designed to produce a COP larger than 2.

, the internal energy flow analysis is a useful tool in the design of a heat pump, in particular, for the case of the single effect ideal machine, as it allows a thorough analysis and understanding of the energy flow within the machine, and the identification of the sources of exergy destruction, as well as the sources of excess exergy production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the internal energy flow analysis is an effective tool for the design of the heat and power systems.
the exergy analysis is the best way to understand and to optimize the internal energy flow distribution within a single-effect sorption heat pump, in order to increase the COP.
the excess exergy is the energy that the machine is not able to transform, but which can be used to improve the efficiency of the process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the excess exergy can only be produced in the heat source and the heat sink.
the excess exergy is not necessarily produced in the heat exchangers, but can also be produced in the sorbent bed or in the evaporator, depending on the process.
the internal energy flow analysis is an efficient method to evaluate the exergy destructions and to identify the bottlenecks in a system.
